chunks: And through him, from Ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Habib al-Sajistani, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Allah the Almighty said: I will surely punish every group of Muslims in Islam that submits to the guardianship of every unjust Imam who is not from Allah, even if that group is pious and God-fearing in their actions; and I will surely forgive every group of Muslims in Islam that submits to the guardianship of every just Imam from Allah, even if that group is sinful and erring in their actions.
ai.seo_question: What is the primary criterion for divine punishment or forgiveness regarding the Imams in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith qudsi from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* underscores the Shia doctrine of *Wilayah* as the foundational axis of faith, prioritizing allegiance to the divinely appointed Imam over individual ritual piety. It illustrates the theological principle that the validity of a community's worship is contingent upon the correctness of their leadership, distinguishing between the 'just' Imam from Allah and the 'unjust' one, thereby linking communal salvation directly to the acceptance of Imamate.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (13) Ibn Mahboob narrated from Hisham bin Salim from Habeeb as-Sajistani that Imam Abu Ja’far as-Sadiq (as) had said:

Allah the Almighty has said: I will torture every group of Muslims that has believed in the guardianship of every imam of injustice even those Muslims are pious and God-fearing and I will forgive every group of Muslims that has believed in the guardianship of every just imam, whose imamate has been determined by Allah, even if these Muslims are guilty and sinful.”
